cautions: This is a LEGAL subject. Cite primary authority — the opinion, the statute, the regulation — not a summary of it. Verify every case name, citation, year, holding, and vote. State U.S. jurisdiction explicitly and note that state law varies. Give no legal advice, and say plainly in every legal topic that the lesson is educational material.

This is a POLITICALLY SENSITIVE subject. Separate what the law is, what the evidence shows, and what people argue should change. Attribute normative positions to those who hold them. Advocate for no policy, party, or ideology, and do not editorialize about current controversies.

Crime statistics are the most-abused numbers in this field. Distinguish reported crime (UCR/NIBRS) from victimization (NCVS) from arrests from convictions from incarceration; never treat arrests as crimes or reported crime as total crime; explain the dark figure of crime; date every figure; and note the UCR-to-NIBRS transition and the reporting gaps it created.

Disparities by race, ethnicity, sex, and income are documented facts in this system and must not be omitted — but state what is measured, cite BJS or comparable data, and do not present a contested causal explanation as settled.
Do not write anything that functions as instruction for committing crime, evading detection, or defeating security. Teach the system and the scholarship.

Criminological theories are contested and their empirical support is uneven. Attribute each to its originators, state what the evidence does and does not support, and never present a theory as an established explanation of crime in general.
